subject: social_science
chapter_title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

concepts.title: French Revolutionary Collective Identity
concepts.definition: Strategies and symbols introduced by French rebels to foster a shared sense of belonging and national unity among the population.
concepts.key_idea: The revolution shifted sovereignty from the crown to a collective body of citizens.
question_patterns: What measures did French revolutionaries take to create a sense of collective identity?
How did the ideas of la patrie and le citoyen contribute to national unity?
Describe the changes in the French flag and the Estates General after 1789.
List the practices used to build a common identity in revolutionary France.
Explain the role of language and hymns in the French nation-building process.

solution_steps.explain: The revolutionaries introduced 'la patrie' (fatherland) and 'le citoyen' (citizen) to emphasize a community with equal rights.
The Estates General was replaced by the National Assembly, and a new tricolour flag was adopted.
Centralized laws were established, internal customs were removed, and French was promoted as the national language.

concepts.title: The Napoleonic Code of 1804
concepts.definition: A comprehensive set of legal reforms that standardized laws, protected property rights, and removed birth-based social hierarchies.
concepts.key_idea: Administrative rationalization and legal equality were exported to French-occupied territories.
question_patterns: What were the main features of the Civil Code of 1804?
How did Napoleon simplify administrative divisions in Europe?
Explain the impact of the Napoleonic Code on the peasantry and businessmen.
Which privileges were abolished by the Napoleonic Code?
Describe the administrative reforms introduced by Napoleon in conquered territories.

solution_steps.explain: The code established equality before the law and secured the right to private property.
It abolished all privileges based on birth and the feudal system of serfdom.
Guild restrictions were removed, and transport and communication systems were upgraded.

concepts.title: Liberal Nationalism
concepts.definition: A 19th-century ideology advocating for individual freedom, equality under the law, and the removal of state-imposed economic restrictions.
concepts.key_idea: Liberalism linked political freedom with the creation of a unified national market.
question_patterns: What did liberalism mean for the new middle classes in the 19th century?
Explain the political and economic aspects of liberal nationalism.
How did the middle class define freedom and equality?
What were the economic demands of liberal nationalists?
Describe the concept of government by consent in liberal ideology.

solution_steps.explain: It stood for representative government, a constitution, and the end of clerical privileges.
It demanded the freedom of markets and the abolition of state restrictions on the movement of capital.

concepts.title: Customs Duty Calculation
concepts.definition: The calculation of total taxes paid by merchants passing through multiple internal customs barriers within the German Confederation.
concepts.key_idea: Standardized economic unions like the Zollverein aimed to eliminate these repetitive costs.
question_patterns: Calculate the total duty for a merchant passing through {number_of_barriers} barriers.
If a merchant pays {tax_rate_percent} percent at each of {number_of_barriers} stops, find the total tax on goods worth {item_value}.
What is the total customs duty for a shipment valued at {item_value} across {number_of_barriers} checkpoints?
Find the cumulative tax for {number_of_barriers} barriers at a rate of {tax_rate_percent} percent.
How much total duty is paid on an item of value {item_value} if the rate is {tax_rate_percent} percent per barrier?

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the item value by the tax rate percentage divided by 100.
Multiply the tax per barrier by the total number of barriers passed.

concepts.title: Treaty of Vienna 1815
concepts.definition: A diplomatic agreement by European powers to restore monarchies and redraw borders to prevent future French expansion after Napoleon's defeat.
concepts.key_idea: The settlement aimed to establish a new conservative order in Europe.
question_patterns: What were the main objectives of the Treaty of Vienna?
How did the Congress of Vienna redraw the map of Europe?
Which dynasties were restored to power after the 1815 settlement?
Describe the territorial changes imposed on France in 1815.
Who hosted the Congress of Vienna and what was its purpose?

solution_steps.explain: The Congress was hosted by Duke Metternich and included Britain, Russia, Prussia, and Austria.
France lost annexed lands; the Netherlands gained Belgium; Prussia and Austria gained new territories.
The Bourbon dynasty was restored to the French throne.

concepts.title: Mazzini and Secret Societies
concepts.definition: The formation of underground political groups by revolutionaries like Giuseppe Mazzini to fight for liberty and unified nation-states.
concepts.key_idea: Secret societies were the primary vehicles for spreading nationalist ideals under autocratic repression.
question_patterns: Who was Giuseppe Mazzini and what were his goals?
Describe the secret societies founded by Mazzini.
Why did Metternich describe Mazzini as a dangerous enemy?
What was the role of Young Italy and Young Europe?
How did Mazzini envision the future of the Italian peninsula?

solution_steps.explain: Giuseppe Mazzini was an Italian revolutionary and member of the Carbonari.
He founded 'Young Italy' in Marseilles and 'Young Europe' in Berne.
He believed in a unified, democratic Italian republic as the basis of liberty.

concepts.title: Greek War of Independence
concepts.definition: A successful nationalist struggle by the Greeks to gain independence from the Ottoman Empire, supported by European intellectuals.
concepts.key_idea: The struggle mobilized nationalist sentiment across the European educated elite.
question_patterns: Explain the significance of the Greek war of independence.
Which treaty recognized Greece as an independent nation?
How did poets and artists support the Greek struggle?
When did the Greek struggle for independence begin?
Why was Greece called the cradle of European civilization?

solution_steps.explain: The struggle began in 1821 against the Ottoman Empire.
West Europeans and poets like Lord Byron provided funds and cultural support.
The Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 recognized Greek independence.

concepts.title: Romantic Nationalism
concepts.definition: A cultural movement that used art, poetry, and folk traditions to create a sense of shared national heritage and identity.
concepts.key_idea: Culture, rather than just war, was vital in shaping the idea of the nation.
question_patterns: What was Romanticism in the context of European nationalism?
How did Johann Gottfried Herder define true German culture?
Explain the role of folk songs and dances in nation-building.
How did language act as a weapon of national resistance in Poland?
Describe the contribution of Karol Kurpinski to Polish nationalism.

solution_steps.explain: Romantics focused on emotions, intuition, and mystical feelings over reason.
Folk songs (das volk), vernacular language, and local folklore were used to reach the masses.

concepts.title: Unification of Germany
concepts.definition: The process of merging various German states into a single empire under Prussian leadership and military strength.
concepts.key_idea: Otto von Bismarck used the army and bureaucracy to achieve unification through three wars.
question_patterns: Briefly trace the process of German unification.
Who was the architect of German unification?
What was the role of Prussia in the making of Germany?
When and where was William I proclaimed German Emperor?
Describe the three wars that led to the unification of Germany.

solution_steps.explain: Otto von Bismarck, the Prussian Chief Minister, was the primary architect.
Three wars were fought over seven years with Austria, Denmark, and France.
Kaiser William I was proclaimed Emperor at Versailles in January 1871.

concepts.title: Unification of Italy
concepts.definition: The political and military movement to unite the fragmented states of the Italian peninsula into a single kingdom.
concepts.key_idea: Unification was achieved through a mix of elite diplomacy and popular revolutionary action.
question_patterns: How was Italy unified in the 19th century?
What was the role of Cavour in Italian unification?
Describe Giuseppe Garibaldi's contribution to the making of Italy.
Which state led the movement for Italian unification?
Who was proclaimed the king of united Italy in 1861?

solution_steps.explain: Sardinia-Piedmont, under King Victor Emmanuel II, led the process.
Chief Minister Cavour secured a strategic alliance with France to defeat Austria.
Garibaldi and his 'Red Shirts' conquered the southern regions with peasant support.

concepts.title: Formation of the British Nation-State
concepts.definition: The long-term political process by which England established dominance over Scotland and Ireland to form the United Kingdom.
concepts.key_idea: The British nation-state was forged through parliamentary acts rather than a sudden revolution.
question_patterns: How was the history of nationalism in Britain different from the rest of Europe?
What was the significance of the Act of Union (1707)?
How did the English parliament seize power from the monarchy?
Describe the incorporation of Ireland into the United Kingdom.
What symbols were used to promote a new British identity?

solution_steps.explain: The English Parliament, after 1688, became the instrument for nation-building.
The Act of Union (1707) joined England and Scotland; Ireland was added in 1801.
English language and symbols like the Union Jack were promoted over local cultures.

concepts.title: National Allegories
concepts.definition: The artistic personification of a nation using female figures to give concrete form to abstract political ideas.
concepts.key_idea: Figures like Marianne and Germania served as visual symbols of national unity and heroism.
question_patterns: Who were Marianne and Germania?
What was the importance of the way national allegories were portrayed?
Explain the symbolism of the crown of oak leaves in Germania's image.
How did artists personify the nation in the 19th century?
What did the broken chain and the sword signify in national imagery?

solution_steps.explain: Marianne represented the French Republic; Germania represented the German nation.
Attributes like the red cap (liberty) and oak leaves (heroism) conveyed specific national values.

concepts.title: Balkan Nationalist Tensions
concepts.definition: The intense ethnic and political conflict in Southeast Europe caused by the decline of the Ottoman Empire and competing imperial interests.
concepts.key_idea: The Balkans became a 'powder keg' that eventually triggered the First World War.
question_patterns: Why did nationalist tensions emerge in the Balkans?
Describe the ethnic composition of the Balkan region.
How did the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire affect the Balkans?
Explain the role of big power rivalry in the Balkan conflict.
Why did the Balkan area become an area of intense conflict after 1871?

solution_steps.explain: The Balkans included modern-day Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, and other Slavic regions.
Subject nationalities broke away from the weakening Ottoman Empire to claim independence.
Rivalries between Russia, Germany, and Britain for control over the region led to war.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A merchant travels from Hamburg to Nuremberg with goods worth {item_value} florins. He passes through {number_of_barriers} customs barriers, paying a {tax_rate_percent} percent duty at each. Calculate the total duty paid.

solution_template.explain: Multiply 1000 by 5/100 to get the tax at one stop.
Multiply the unit tax by 11 barriers.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What is the total customs duty for a shipment valued at {item_value} units passing through {number_of_barriers} barriers at a {tax_rate_percent} percent rate?

solution_template.explain: Multiply the unit tax by 5 barriers.
